question: In **Soweto Retail Hub Ltd**, director **Ndlovu** owned **590,000** shares out of **1,250,000** total issued shares. The company repurchased **155,000** shares from other discontented shareholders and cancelled them. Ndlovu did not participate in the repurchase. Calculate the change in **Ndlovu's percentage shareholding**:
wrong_answers_pool: Remained unchanged at 47.20% because Ndlovu bought no shares
explanation:
Original Shareholding % = (590,000 / 1,250,000) x 100 = 47.20%
New Total Shares = 1,250,000 - 155,000 = 1,095,000 shares
New Shareholding % = (590,000 / 1,095,000) x 100 = 53.88%
Net Change = 53.88% - 47.20% = Increased by 6.68% (from 47.20% to 53.88%). Notice: Without investing a single cent of personal money, Ndlovu's voting power increased significantly!

tags.learning_outcome: Evaluate change in shareholding for Ndlovu in Soweto Retail Hub Ltd

question: The financial indicators of **Apex Auto Ltd** reflect a **Current Ratio of 2.2 : 1** and an **Acid-Test Ratio of 1.2 : 1**. The Balance Sheet discloses Current Liabilities of **R820,000**. Reverse-engineer the exact carrying value of **Trading Inventory**:

question: The Tangible Asset records of **Laysano Ltd** show: Carrying Value at 1 March (opening): **R3,800,000**; Carrying Value at 28 February (closing): **R4,450,000**. During the year, depreciation amounted to **R320,000** and an old asset with a carrying value of **R140,000** was sold. Calculate the **Cost of Tangible Assets Purchased (Additions)**:
wrong_answers_pool: R650,000 (simply took the net difference without accounting for depreciation or disposals)
R970,000 (forgot to add back disposals carrying value)
explanation: Asset Note reconstruction: Closing CV (R4,450,000) = Opening CV (R3,800,000) + Additions - Depreciation (R320,000) - Disposals (R140,000). Additions = R4,450,000 - R3,800,000 + R320,000 + R140,000 = R1,110,000 (Investing Outflow).

question: **Paarl Packaging Ltd** repurchased **32,000** ordinary shares from an existing shareholder at **R10.20** per share. R288,000.00 (used new issue price instead of weighted average)

question: **Orchid Ltd** disposed of a **Delivery Truck** on **30 November** (9 months into the financial year ending 28 February). Original cost price: **R420,000**; Accumulated depreciation at the start of the year (1 March): **R168,000**. Depreciation rate: **20% p.a. on diminishing balance**. The asset was sold on credit to a dealer for **R210,000**. Calculate the carrying value on the date of disposal and the resulting profit or loss on sale:
correct_answer: Carrying Value = R214,200; LOSS on sale = R4,200
wrong_answers_pool: Carrying Value = R252,000; PROFIT on sale = R42,000 (forgot current year depreciation)
Carrying Value = R420,000; LOSS on sale = R210,000
Carrying Value = R214,200; PROFIT on sale = R4,200 (inverted profit and loss)
Carrying Value = R235,620; Profit on sale = R6,300
Carrying Value = R205,800; Loss on sale = R4,200
Carrying Value = R214,200; Zero profit or loss
Carrying Value = R210,000; Profit on sale = R37,800
explanation: 1. Current year depreciation up to sale (30 November, 9 months): R37,800. 2. Total accumulated depreciation at date of disposal: R168,000 + R37,800 = R205,800. 3. Carrying value at date of disposal: Cost (R420,000) - Accumulated Depreciation (R205,800) = R214,200. 4. Profit/Loss on disposal: Selling price (R210,000) - Carrying value (R214,200) = Carrying Value = R214,200; LOSS on sale = R4,200.

question: The records of **Sandton Goods Ltd** show: Shareholders for Dividends on 1 March (opening): **R410,000**; Interim dividends paid during the year: **R270,000**; Final dividends recommended at year-end (closing): **R480,000**. question: The records of **Kairo Furnishers Ltd** show Debtors Control of **R520,000** and Provision for Bad Debts of **R26,000**. An insolvent debtor who owes **R25,000** must be written off as irrecoverable. The provision must then be adjusted to **5% of good debtors**.
